sources.note: Nothing. "Wasu (Waçu, Wassú) is an extinct and unattested, presumed language of the Serra do Azul in Joaquim Gomes, Alagoas, Brazil." Only further reading: Fabre 2005.

sources.citation: Instituto Socioambiental, Povos Indígenas no Brasil, verbete "Wassu" (published 01/2014, modified 2018-07-13).
sources.note: Nothing. "O verbete sobre esse povo indígena ainda não existe!"; the 'Família linguística' field is empty; population AL 2014 (Siasi/Sesai).

sources.citation: Wikipedia (pt), "Wassu-Cocal" (people article), quoting Moseley, Christopher (ed.) 2007, Encyclopedia of the World's Endangered Languages, p. 180.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Quotes Moseley 2007 p.180: "All 1,447 (1999) Wassu are native speakers of Portuguese today and the language they possibly spoke is extinct." The article's own unsourced claim that the mother tongue is 'tupi antigo' is contradicted by every linguistic source (unattested, filiation unknown).

sources.citation: Fabre, Alain (2005-; entry last modified 2009-10-09). "Wassú". Diccionario etnolingüístico y guía bibliográfica de los pueblos indígenas sudamericanos, p. 1.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or any linguistic feature: "Lengua de filiación lingüística desconocida por falta de datos. Hoy todos hablan portugués." Not cited in Loukotka 1968, Tovar & Larrucea de Tovar 1984 or Nimuendajú 1946; may be a composite group of diverse ethnic origin. Bibliography lists only ethnohistorical items (Carvalho 1984, 1988; CEDI 1983; Dantas, Sampaio & Carvalho 1998; Ferreira 1991; Nimuendajú 1946 map).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid wasu1238 "Wasu" (Hammarström, Forkel, Haspelmath & Bank), page + JSON record.
sources.note: Nothing. Classification = Unattested; AES status extinct (Ethnologue 2025: 'Wasu (wsu-wsu) = 9 (Dormant)'). Only two references, both MED 'wordlist_or_less': Dantas, Sampaio & Carvalho 1998 (overview, 2 pp.) and Ferreira 1991 (type unknown). No grammar, sketch or phonology reference exists.

sources.citation: Moseley, Christopher (ed.). 2007. Encyclopedia of the World's Endangered Languages. London/New York: Routledge, p. 180 (Wassu entry, South America section by Mily Crevels).
